fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into Your Proof Approvals
fields.features_subheading: Every job keeps its proofs and each reviewer's decision in one record you can search.
fields.feature_1:
A request form that opens each job

Emergent builds the request form and the job database from your prompt. Each request saves the client, the item, the due date, and the source files as one job in a database you own.
fields.feature_2:
Numbered proofs that keep comments

Every upload becomes the next version of the proof, v1 then v2 then v3. Comments and decisions stay on the version they were made on, and a reviewer can open any earlier round.
fields.feature_3:
Reviewers in the order you set

You name who approves each kind of job and in what order. The app sends a proof to the next reviewer only after the one before approves it, and a rejection sends it back to design.
fields.feature_4:
Reminders when a proof sits too long

The app sends a Slack or email reminder when a proof waits past the time you set for that reviewer. If it still has no decision, the app escalates it to the manager you named.
fields.feature_5:
Only the approved file goes to print

When the last reviewer approves, the app emails the printer a link to that version and no other. Earlier proofs stay in the job history, each one marked as replaced by the next.
fields.feature_6:
Your code, with no per-approver seats

Add every client, designer, and reviewer a job needs, with no per-approver seats to count. On paid plans you can export the full code of the app to your GitHub repository.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Teams and the Proofs They Sign Off
fields.tab_content_1:
Label v3 waits for its third approver

Saffronhill Foods sends every new label to its design lead first, then its regulatory reviewer, then its brand manager. Version 3 of the 12 oz salsa label has 2 of its 3 approvals. Brand manager Corwenna Strouden gets a Slack direct message with a link to v3, and the printer gets no file until she approves.
fields.tab_content_2:
Order #2316 goes to press when Aurelian approves

Gorsebrook Print Co. emails each customer a proof link before a screen is burned. Aurelian Edevane opens proof v2 for order #2316, 48 shirts in 2 ink colors, on his phone and taps Approve. The app saves his approval on v2 and moves the order into the press queue.
fields.tab_content_3:
Round 3 waits for Rosmund before any design work

Pellgrave Studio's contract with Fellwater Outfitters covers 2 revision rounds on a set of 6 web banners. When the client asks for round 3, the app holds the request and emails account manager Rosmund Delacombe. No designer sees the new changes until she approves the extra round.
fields.tab_content_4:
Four signs with a price also go to pricing

Harrowfield Grocers prints 22 spring signs for its 14 stores, and marketing approves all 22. The 4 signs that show a price also go to pricing analyst Tiberius Wolstenholme by Slack direct message. The app releases the 18 signs without a price to the printer now and the other 4 once he approves.

fields.howto_title: How to Build an Artwork Approval Process
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to set the reviewers, rules, and printer release for an artwork approval process, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Name the reviewers for each job type
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Decide what counts as a new version
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down every kind of artwork your team signs off: labels, customer proofs, client banners, store signs. For each one, note who asks for it, which files come with it, and the date it must reach the printer. Each kind becomes a job type in the app.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Name the people who review each kind of job and the order they sign in. Mark any reviewer who only checks some pieces, such as a regulatory check on food labels. Each name becomes a step, and a rejection at any step sends the proof back.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Decide when an upload starts a new version and when it only fixes a file inside the current round. Write down how many revision rounds each contract includes and who signs off on one more, before a designer spends time on it.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Choose how long a proof can wait with each reviewer before a reminder goes out, and who hears about it next if nothing changes. Pick Slack or email for each person, based on where they already read their requests.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Describe the app in one prompt
fields.howto_step_5_des: Open Emergent and describe the process in plain English: the request fields, the job types, the reviewer order, the reminders, and the printer release. Emergent builds the app from that description, and you change any step later by prompting again.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Connect the tools your team uses
fields.howto_step_6_des: Connect Slack for direct messages and the email account that sends customer proof links. If your project tracker or print vendor portal has an API, the app can send each approved job and its status there as well.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Run one live job through the app
fields.howto_step_7_des: Run one real job through the app before you switch over, with a comment and a rejection on v1 and an approval on v2. Check that each reviewer got the right message, that the comments stayed on v1, and that the printer received v2 only.

faq_plan.q: What is an artwork approval process?
faq_plan.a: An artwork approval process is the set of steps a design passes through before it is printed or published. Someone requests the work, a designer sends a proof, named people review it in turn, and each change becomes a new version. It ends when one approved version goes to the printer.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an artwork approval process?
faq_plan.a: Start by listing each kind of artwork you approve and who must sign off on it, in order. Then describe that process in plain English to Emergent's AI automation builder, which builds the app from your prompt. Run one test job before your team uses it.

faq_plan.q: What steps should an artwork approval process include?
faq_plan.a: Plan for five steps: a request with the brief and source files, a numbered proof, review in a set order, revisions saved as new versions, and release of the approved file. Add a regulatory or pricing check only for the pieces that need one.

faq_plan.q: Who should sign off in an artwork approval process for packaging?
faq_plan.a: Give sign-off to the people who answer for each part of the package: a designer for layout, a regulatory reviewer for the required text, and a brand manager for the final look. Put the regulatory check before the brand review, so a text fix never reopens an approved design.

faq_plan.q: How many revision rounds should an artwork approval process allow?
faq_plan.a: Allow the number of rounds your price covers, and write it into the contract for each deliverable. Decide in advance who approves a round past that number. Then the app counts each change request against the limit and holds the one that goes over it.

faq_plan.q: How do you track proof versions in an artwork approval process?
faq_plan.a: Give every upload a version number and keep each comment attached to the version it was written on. Name files the same way each time, such as the job number plus v1 or v2, so anyone can match a printed piece to its proof. In an app Emergent builds, every version and comment is saved in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: What should a customer check during an artwork approval process?
faq_plan.a: A customer should check spelling, phone numbers, dates, colors, sizes, quantities, and logo placement before approving. Put each item on the approval screen as a box to tick, and save the customer's name and the time with the approval.

faq_plan.q: How long should each reviewer get in an artwork approval process?
faq_plan.a: Give each reviewer a time that fits your print date, such as one business day for your own team and two for customers. Send a reminder when that time passes and escalate to a manager after a second one. The app sends the reminders and escalations for you, and the workflow has no task cap.

faq_plan.q: Can customers approve proofs from a phone in an artwork approval process?
faq_plan.a: Yes, as long as the proof link opens a page built for a phone screen. Show the proof large enough to read the fine print, put the order details beside it, and offer two choices: approve, or ask for changes with a comment. Emergent builds that page with the rest of the app, with no per-approver seats for your customers.

faq_plan.q: How does an artwork approval process get the right file to the printer?
faq_plan.a: It releases the file from one place, and only after the last approval. Send the printer a link to the approved version instead of an email attachment, and ask them to confirm the version number on the job ticket. If a reprint comes up months later, the job history shows which version was printed.

This page shows the approval app a team builds around its own artwork: a request form that opens a job, numbered versions that keep their comments, reviewers in a set order with a rule for who must approve which piece, reminders and escalations, and a release step that sends the printer only the approved version. Four real segments carry it: packaging labels, print shop customer proofs, agency client rounds and multi-store retail signage.
